suggested_issue_title: 35 of 45 files under src/aspose_tex/ fail to parse (IndentationError) at HEAD, including the presentation entry point
suggested_issue_body:
## Summary

Most of this repository's own Python source under `src/aspose_tex/` does not parse as valid Python. The module the package's own docstring names as the user-facing entry point is among the files that fail.

## Environment

- Repository: aspose-tex-foss/Aspose.TeX-FOSS-for-Python
- Revision: `181015d2eee3e19f8af3d84e4a932ac84ad47c7c` (default branch `main`)
- Tool: Python's standard `ast.parse` (reproducible with any Python 3 interpreter; no third-party tooling involved)

## Steps to reproduce

For any `.py` file under `src/aspose_tex/`, run:

```python
import ast
ast.parse(open(path, encoding="utf-8").read())
```

## Actual result

35 of the 45 `.py` files under `src/aspose_tex/` raise `IndentationError`. For example, `src/aspose_tex/presentation/__init__.py`:

```
IndentationError: expected an indented block after function definition on line 107 (line 108)
```

The same shape (`expected an indented block after ...`) recurs across every failing file - the source's indentation is collapsed to one space per level throughout, rather than each file's own apparent intended indentation.

## Files affected (not exhaustive - 35 of 45 total)

`src/aspose_tex/presentation/__init__.py`, `src/aspose_tex/_engine/interpreter.py`, `src/aspose_tex/_engine/nodes.py`, `src/aspose_tex/_input/tokenizer.py`, `src/aspose_tex/_fonts/font_manager.py`, and 30 others under `_engine/`, `_fonts/`, `_input/`, and `_output/`.

## Impact noted for context

`src/aspose_tex/presentation/__init__.py` - the module whose own docstring calls it the user-facing entry point, and which defines `TeXJob`, `TeXOptions`, and the `OutputDevice` hierarchy - does not parse, so the package cannot be imported at all from this source tree at this revision.
